name: Hayward Gallery (Southbank Centre)
funding: £38M Southbank Centre operating budget. Arts Council England National Portfolio Organisation (NPO), admissions, and Southbank Centre trust.
watch: Part of the Southbank Centre, Europe's largest arts centre, on London's South Bank. It has severed conflicting commercial naming deals and follows a statutory public arts charter.

name: Hayy Jameel
funding: Arts complex opened 6 Dec 2021, built and run by Art Jameel and paid for by the Jameel family (Abdul Latif Jameel, a car distribution and diversified group)
watch: Private family-funded arts complex with Saudi Arabia's first independent cinema. Separate site from Jameel Arts Centre in Dubai.
records_note: Hayy Jameel and its parent Art Jameel publish no annual reports, accounts or funder list; the site lists staff and the founder but no board.

name: Henie Onstad Kunstsenter
funding: NOK 45M. Norwegian Ministry of Culture, Viken fylkeskommune, Bærum municipality.
watch: Public foundation with explicit fossil fuel sponsorship exclusion.

name: Henry Moore Institute
funding: Part of the Henry Moore Foundation, funded from its investment portfolio. Leeds City Council gives £145,743 a year to the Institute; Arts Council England funds the Yorkshire Sculpture International partnership.
watch: The Foundation holds a restricted fund for Bloomberg Connects. 260 UK artists asked five London theatres to drop Bloomberg in May 2026; not targeted here.
records_note: Part of the Henry Moore Foundation, which posts reviews from 2010-11, trustees' reports and accounts 2015 to 2024, and its trustees; no funder list.

name: Heydar Aliyev Center
funding: A US$250M Azerbaijani state project opened in 2012; its main contractor was tied to the Aliyev family's offshore network.
watch: Zaha Hadid building named for Heydar Aliyev; site cleared by forced evictions.
records_note: The centre's site carries no annual reports, accounts, sponsor list or board; it publishes only a statute and structure page for this state body.

name: HIAP (Helsinki International Artist Programme)
funding: Arts Promotion Centre Finland (Taike), City of Helsinki, Kone Foundation; non-profit artists' association.

name: Hiroshima City Museum of Contemporary Art
funding: FY2024 report: City of Hiroshima, plus grants from the Agency for Cultural Affairs, Ogasawara Foundation and Asahi Shimbun Foundation.
watch: Municipal museum. Chim↑Pom's solo show was cancelled after their Oct 2008 'Pika' skywriting over Hiroshima drew public backlash. A 2026 Mel Chin show is co-run with Asahi Shimbun.
records_note: The city museum posts yearly reports for FY2017 to FY2024 that credit funders per show, but shows no accounts and no board list.
sources: https://www.e-flux.com/announcements/?i=Hiroshima City Museum of Contemporary Art (Hiroshima MOCA)

name: Hartware MedienKunstVerein (HMKV)
funding: City of Dortmund, Kunststiftung NRW, State of North Rhine-Westphalia; non-profit art association.

name: Holburne Museum
funding: Public funders are the National Lottery Heritage Fund and Community Fund. Trusts include Garfield Weston, AKO, Clore Duffield and the Blavatnik Family Foundation; Bloomberg Philanthropies backed the website.
watch: Bloomberg Philanthropies listed for digital support.
records_note: Posts trustees' reports and signed accounts for 2016 to 2024, names its eleven directors and keeps a named supporters list with no date.

name: HOME
funding: £7.2M income (FY2025); Arts Council England and Manchester City Council core funding.
watch: Censorship row: in Mar 2024 it cancelled a Gaza writing event, then reversed the decision after protest.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the Charity Commission register, the Our Supporters page names funders and patrons undated, and trustees are listed.

name: Hong-gah Museum
funding: Founder Chiu Tsai-hsing's private money through Chew's Culture Foundation. No admission fee; running cost about NT$14M a year (2006).
watch: Chiu's money is from electronics firms, among them Jiye Enterprise. The 2006 Global Views article is the latest funding account found.
records_note: Its site publishes no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board; it names only founder Andrew Chew and Chew's Culture Foundation.
